title: How to Keep Herb Scissors Sharp and Rust Free
meta_description: Stop struggling with dull blades. Learn how to maintain herb scissors to prevent rust and keep your multi-blade shears cutting sharp for years.
html:
There is nothing more frustrating than reaching for your herb shears only to find they’re crushing your basil instead of slicing it. Multi-blade scissors are a game-changer for meal prep, but because they have more surface area and tight crevices, they require a bit more attention than a standard pair of kitchen shears. If you want to maintain herb scissors so they glide through cilantro and chives for years, you need a system for cleaning and storage.

The Secret to Immediate Cleaning

The biggest enemy of sharp blades is residue. When small bits of herb stem and leaf get trapped between the five blades, they dry out and create a sticky film. This film doesn't just make the scissors messy; it acts as a magnet for moisture, which leads to oxidation and rust.

The most efficient way to handle this is by using a tool designed for the job. If you use the Herb Scissors, they come with a dedicated cleaning comb. This is essential because it allows you to clear out the debris from between the blades without risking a finger cut. After every use, run the comb through the blades to lift out the trapped greens before rinsing.

How to Maintain Herb Scissors and Prevent Rust

Rust happens when iron, oxygen, and moisture meet. Since most high-quality herb shears are made of stainless steel, they are resistant, but not immune, to corrosion—especially if they sit in a damp sink or are tossed into a crowded dishwasher.

To keep your blades pristine, follow these steps:

  • Hand wash only: Dishwasher detergents are often abrasive and the high heat can dull the fine edge of the blades.
  • Dry immediately: Never let your scissors air dry. Use a clean kitchen towel to wipe every single blade dry immediately after washing.
  • Avoid acidic soak: Don't leave your shears soaking in lemon juice or vinegar-heavy liquids, as the acid can eat away at the protective finish of the steel.

Sharpening Multi-Blade Shears

Standard whetstones are difficult to use on five-blade scissors because you can't easily access the inner edges. For most home cooks, the best way to maintain the edge is through prevention and light maintenance.

If you notice the blades are starting to pull rather than cut, you can use a fine-grit diamond sharpening rod. Carefully slide the rod along the beveled edge of each blade, moving from the pivot point toward the tip. Do this in one direction only—don't saw back and forth, as this can create microscopic burrs on the metal that actually make the scissors feel duller.

Proper Storage for Long-Term Edge Retention

How you store your tools is just as important as how you clean them. If you throw your Herb Scissors into a "junk drawer" with other metal utensils, the blades will clink against other tools. These tiny impacts create nicks in the metal, which ruins the clean slicing action.

Store your shears in a dedicated slot in a knife block, or hang them from a magnetic strip. If a drawer is your only option, consider a simple neoprene sleeve or a dedicated plastic case. This keeps the blades protected from impact and prevents them from rubbing against other cutlery.

Dealing with Stuck Blades

Over time, you might find that the tension in your scissors feels off or the blades aren't closing perfectly. This is usually caused by a buildup of minerals from hard water or stubborn sap from woody herbs like rosemary.

To fix this, apply a tiny drop of food-grade mineral oil to the pivot screw. Open and close the scissors several times to work the oil into the joint. This reduces friction and ensures that the force of your squeeze is distributed evenly across all five blades, which prevents uneven wear and tear on the edges.

FAQ

Can I put my herb scissors in the dishwasher?

It is highly recommended that you avoid the dishwasher. The harsh chemicals and extreme heat can degrade the temper of the steel and lead to premature rusting in the pivot joint.

How often should I sharpen my herb shears?

If you are using them a few times a week and cleaning them properly, you likely only need to touch up the edges once a year. If you notice they are bruising the herbs rather than cutting them, it's time for a sharpen.

What is the best way to remove existing rust spots?

For small rust spots, make a thick paste of baking soda and water. Apply it to the spot, let it sit for 15 minutes, and scrub gently with a soft toothbrush. Rinse and dry immediately, then apply a thin layer of food-grade mineral oil to seal the metal.
